First release: an MCP server that lets an AI agent (Codex, Claude Code, Cursor…) run, watch and drive Solar2D projects in the Solar2D Simulator. One Windows exe, nothing else to install (no Python, no Node). Tested against Solar2D **2026.3729**.

**Download** `solar2d-mcp.exe` (or the zip, which also has the README and licence), put it somewhere like `C:\Tools\solar2d-mcp\`, then:

```
codex mcp add solar2d -- C:\Tools\solar2d-mcp\solar2d-mcp.exe
```

The README has the `config.toml` version, and `--simulator <path>` if the simulator isn't installed in the default place.

**Tools**
- `run_project`, `relaunch`, `stop`, `status`
- `read_logs`: print() output and runtime errors with stack traces, live
- `screenshot`, `display_tree` (every object: name, widget type, text, bounds, listeners, composer scene)
- `tap` (with `hold_ms` for long presses), `drag`, `key`
- `touch_down` / `touch_move` / `touch_up`: fingers that stay down between calls (press and hold, multi-touch)
- `type_text`: types into native text fields with the same userInput events as a keyboard
- `answer_alert`: native.showAlert appears as an in-app overlay the agent can see and press
- `wait_for`: a Lua condition and/or a log line
- `eval_lua`: read or change anything in the running app

Tested with every `widget` library widget. This build was tested under Wine on Linux; it hasn't been run on real Windows yet, so please report anything odd.
